Star Wars.name: Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope
Star Wars.standIn: The original 1977 film, standing in for the whole saga

Microsoft Office.name: Microsoft365
Microsoft Office.standIn: Microsoft 365, the renamed successor to Microsoft Office

Star Wars.reason: Universally known; Yoda speech is meme-familiar, though millennials love it more.

Microsoft Office.reason: Students live in Word for essays; everyone gets the pun.

Game of Thrones.reason: Ended when they were young teens; known by name, not watched widely.

Twitter.reason: Known, but they're on TikTok and Instagram; 140-character limit feels ancient.

Arnold Schwarzenegger.reason: Recognizable name and accent, but his heyday predates them entirely.

Microsoft Windows.reason: Everyone uses Windows, but Vista's reputation is before their time.

Rick Astley.reason: Rickroll is internet canon for this crowd, even if the music isn't.

Pixar.reason: Grew up on Pixar; strong nostalgic affection in this room.

Up.reason: A childhood staple; the opening montage is famously beloved.

50 Cent.reason: Known via memes and birthday song, but his peak was 2003.

Nickelback.reason: They know the 'photograph' meme; the hate-joke is a millennial bit.

Breaking Bad.reason: Still huge on streaming and memes; pizza-on-roof scene is iconic.

Jeopardy!.reason: They know the format, but it's their grandparents' show.

Lego.reason: Universal childhood toy; stepping-on-Lego pain is a shared meme.

Tetris.reason: Everyone knows Tetris; the tetanus pun reads instantly.

Terminator 2: Judgment Day.reason: Catchphrase survives by osmosis, but few have actually watched the film.

Jeopardy!.note: The joke needs a quiz show where people win money for answers, and none that fit (Millionaire, Family Feud, Are You Smarter Than a 5th Grader?) lands better with this crowd; the shows they do like are talent contests that would break the joke.
